# Calculate changes in water quality

This script takes inundation area time series output from other analyses to estimate the volume of water exchanged on an average tide, and therefore the average volume of water that would undergo denitrification and contribute to changed water quality in the channel.

## 1. Inputs

First, load relevant packages.

```{r get_packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(pracma)
library(lubridate)

# also turn off scientific notation (personal preference)
options(scipen = 999)
```

Next, input datasets. These are output from the GenerateBatchRMAResults scripts.

Inundation data.

S1, S2, etc refer to Scenario 1, Scenario 2, etc.

```{r load_inundation_data}
# make a function to keep relevant data - time related and inundation area data
keeprelevant <- function(dataset){
  dataset %>% 
  dplyr::select(!contains("creek")) %>% 
    dplyr::select(c("Timestep", "Day", "Hour", contains("area")))
}

Inun_S1 <- read_csv(here("Output/csv/run0086_summary.csv"))[,-1] %>% keeprelevant()
Inun_S2 <- read_csv(here("Output/csv/run0083a_summary.csv"))[,-1] %>% keeprelevant()
Inun_S3 <- read_csv(here("Output/csv/run0087_summary.csv"))[,-1] %>% keeprelevant()
Inun_S4 <- read_csv(here("Output/csv/run0093a_summary.csv"))[,-1] %>% keeprelevant()

Inun_S8 <- read_csv(here("Output/csv/run0092a_summary.csv"))[,-1] %>% keeprelevant()
```

Flow velocity data (to calculate the amount of water exchanged in each tide & the proportion coming to Yandina creek compared to other creeks). These data were extracted from RMA results. I'm not inputting any data from the Southern Natural Area because all of its flows go to Coolum Creek and Maroochy River, so it's not relevant for our Yandina Creek calculations.

Data are stored in the "flow" column and are in m3/s, so need to be converted appropriately to calculate total volumes.

Note, I drew all continuity lines in the wrong direction, so flows entering a wetland are shown as negative values, and vice versa. These is reversed when calculating volumes with the negative sign below.

```{r load_velocity_data}
# function for keeping relevant flow cols & creating a flow column for total volume flowing for the full 15 mins 
# also cut dataset to the middle 28 days used for modelling
keeprelevantflow <- function(dataset){
  dataset %>% 
    dplyr::select("Time","Flow") %>% 
    mutate(Flow_m3_15min = -Flow * 60 * 15,
           Time = dmy_hm(Time)) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(Time > "2023-01-17 00:00:00") %>% 
    dplyr::filter(Time < "2023-02-14 00:00:00")
}
```

## 2. Data analysis

### 2.1 Change in in-channel water quality

**NOTE WE ARE EXCLUDING THESE CHANNEL CALCULATIONS FOR THE PAPER. INCLUDED HERE FOR REFERENCE/COMPARISON IN THE CASE CHANNEL SOIL ORGANIC CARBON DATA WERE AVAILABLE AND PRESENCE OF AQUATIC VEGETATION WAS KNOWN.**

If we assume that the channel is also undertaking denitrification, in addition to the floodplains, we need to calculate how much denitrification occurs within the channel.

We know the area of the channel is 44600 m2. We know that denitrification acts on 0.5 m depth, so 22300 m3 of the water in the channel is undergoing denitrification. For the denitrification equation, we just need the area though.

We will have to assume that we can take soil OC% as the low elevation value (even though it's a much lower elevation in the channel).

Therefore, the denitrification equation is, with a 0.076 mg/L input and a value of 9 for soil organic carbon in low elevations:

Log10 (denitrification, mg/m2/h) = 0.6975 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))

Rearrange for denitrification and substitute numbers in:

```{r channel_denitrification}
10^(0.6975  * log10(0.076) + 1.6030  + (0.0062*9))

# this is denitrification in mg/m2/g. We have an area of 44600 m2 and 12 hours, therefore:

channel_denit_potential_mg <- 10^(0.6975 * log10(0.076) + 1.6030 + (0.0062*9)) * 44600 * 12 # this is the volume that the channel could denitrify
channel_base_nit_vol_mg <- 44600 * 0.5 * 1000 * 0.076 # this is the volume of NOx actually contained in the channel (area x depth x multiplier x concentration). have to multiply the volume by 1000 to convert from m3 to L

# calculate final NOx concnetration in the channel base - change in NOx volume over total volume in the base of the channel
channel_base_nit_final_conc <- (channel_base_nit_vol_mg - channel_denit_potential_mg)/(44600*0.5*1000)

# negative value, therefore with this denitrification rate, the channel could remove all nitrate in the base of the channel
```

Also calculate this for theoretical scenarios with input concentrations of 0.05305 and 0.1, respectively.

```{r channel_denit_other_inputs}
# input concentration of 0.05305
channel_0.05305_denit_potential_mg <- 10^(0.6975 * (log(0.05305)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062*9)) * 44600 * 12 # this is the volume that the channel could denitrify
channel_0.05305_base_nit_vol_mg <- 44600 * 0.5 * 1000 * 0.05305 # this is the volume of NOx actually contained in the channel (area x depth x multiplier x concentration). have to multiply the volume by 1000 to convert from m3 to L

# calculate final NOx concnetration in the channel base - change in NOx volume over total volume in the base of the channel
channel_0.05305_base_nit_final_conc <- (channel_0.05305_base_nit_vol_mg - channel_0.05305_denit_potential_mg)/(44600*0.5*1000)

# this is negative, meaning the potential was greater than the volume. therefore reset the concentration to zero
channel_0.05305_base_nit_final_conc <- 0


# input concentration of 0.1
channel_0.1_denit_potential_mg <- 10^(0.6975 * (log(0.1)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062*9)) * 44600 * 12 # this is the volume that the channel could denitrify
channel_0.1_base_nit_vol_mg <- 44600 * 0.5 * 1000 * 0.1 # this is the volume of NOx actually contained in the channel (area x depth x multiplier x concentration). have to multiply the volume by 1000 to convert from m3 to L

# calculate final NOx concnetration in the channel base - change in NOx volume over total volume in the base of the channel
channel_0.1_base_nit_final_conc <- (channel_0.1_base_nit_vol_mg - channel_0.1_denit_potential_mg)/(44600*0.5*1000)
```

### 2.2 Change in floodplain water quality

First, identify peaks and troughs in the area datasets - we'll use these to calculate the average volume of water exchange in each wetland each tide.

-   use the findpeaks function in the pracma package to find peaks and troughs (negative peaks) in each series - these are the low and high tide volumes

-   we care about all peaks and troughs, regardless of magnitude. Where it turns around represents a change in tide. However, sometimes the data jump a little around, and we don't want this many points to be identified as potential peaks. So need to have a small threshold value. Visually, it looks like all peaks and troughs are at the very least +-50 m3, and at least 20 timesteps apart between successive peaks or troughs, so let's make those the thresholds (this also creates a time series that always alternates between peaks and troughs, rather than multiple of one in a row, which wouldn't make sense).

First, test the method on a single dataset. One of the channel/floodplain connections at 1a in Scenario 3.

```{r test_peaks_troughs}
# visualise what a dataset looks like
ggplot(scen3_TL_cc, aes(x = Time, y = Flow_m3_15min)) +
  geom_line()
# closer inspection of first 200 points
ggplot(scen3_TL_cc[1:200,], aes(x = Time, y = Flow_m3_15min)) +
  geom_line() 

# identify peaks and troughs
peaks <- findpeaks(scen3_TL_cc$Flow_m3_15min, minpeakheight = 50, minpeakdistance = 20)
troughs <- -findpeaks(-scen3_TL_cc$Flow_m3_15min, minpeakheight = 50, minpeakdistance = 20) # feed in negative data to find troughs. making them negative again with the negative in front of the function

# we actually care about volume exchange each tide, not difference in flow rate.
# can use the number of peaks identified to determine the average input and output flow. input flow is summing all positive velocities (total volume in over the 28 days) and dividing by the number of peaks (number of high tides)
positives <- scen3_TL_cc %>% dplyr::filter(Flow_m3_15min>0)
negatives <- scen3_TL_cc %>% dplyr::filter(Flow_m3_15min<0)

table2 <- tibble(ntides = nrow(peaks),
                 tide_vol_in = sum(positives$Flow_m3_15min) / nrow(peaks),
                 tide_vol_out = sum(negatives$Flow_m3_15min) / nrow(troughs),
                 tide_net_exchange = tide_vol_in + tide_vol_out)

    # also calculate the average duration of each high tide as the amount of time that denitrification can act on the water (the duration of low tides is the amount of time denitrification can act on water sitting on the wetland at low tide, so is also important). Each row in the positives/negatives dataframes represents 15 minutes, so divide the number of rows by 4 to get the number of hours, and then divide this by the number of peaks to get the average duration (in hours) of each high or low tide
  table2$peaktime <- nrow(positives)/4/nrow(peaks)
  table2$troughtime <- nrow(negatives)/4/nrow(troughs)
  
ggplot(Inun_S3[1:200,], aes(x = Timestep, y = `1A_area_m2`)) +
  geom_line() 
ggplot(scen3_TL_cc[1:200,], aes(x = Time, y = Flow_m3_15min)) +
  geom_line() 
```

Make this into a function

```{r peaks_function}
peaks_function <- function(dataset){
  # identify peaks and troughs
  peaks <- findpeaks(dataset$Flow_m3_15min, minpeakheight = 50, minpeakdistance = 20)
  troughs <- -findpeaks(-dataset$Flow_m3_15min, minpeakheight = 50, minpeakdistance = 20) # feed in negative data to find troughs. making them negative again with the negative in front of the function

  # we care about volume exchange each tide
  # can use the number of peaks identified to determine the average input and output flow. input flow is summing all positive velocities (total volume in over the 28 days) and dividing by the number of peaks (number of high tides)

  positives <- dataset %>% dplyr::filter(Flow_m3_15min>0)
  negatives <- dataset %>% dplyr::filter(Flow_m3_15min<0)

  # standardise this. rather than dividing by the number of peaks and troughs, just divide by 53, or the expected number of high/low tides during this period. This means that datasets that sometimes don't have a tidal signal still get their tide_vol_in calculated as the average of tides with a tidal signal and tides without.
  table2 <- tibble(ntides = nrow(peaks),
                   tide_vol_in = sum(positives$Flow_m3_15min) / 53,
                 tide_vol_out = sum(negatives$Flow_m3_15min) / 53,
                 tide_net_exchange = tide_vol_in + tide_vol_out)
  
  return(table2)

}
```

Now execute function for each dataset. Note, the function does not output plots, just the calculation of the difference between peaks and troughs. Would need to edit for it to do that.

Calculate the proportion of exchanged volume occurring at Yandina Creek (compared to Coolum Creek).

Create blocks for each scenario.

Scenario 3 (test scenario)

```{r execute_peaks_function_scenario_3}
# scenario 3 - 1a
S3_1a_CC1 <- peaks_function(scen3_TL_cc)
S3_1a_CC2 <- peaks_function(scen3_TR_cc)
S3_1a_YC1 <- peaks_function(scen3_BL_yc)
S3_1a_YC2 <- peaks_function(scen3_BR_yc)

S3_1a_CC_in_per_tide <- (S3_1a_CC1$tide_vol_in + S3_1a_CC2$tide_vol_in)
S3_1a_YC_in_per_tide <- (S3_1a_YC1$tide_vol_in + S3_1a_YC2$tide_vol_in)
S3_1a_CC_out_per_tide <- (S3_1a_CC1$tide_vol_out + S3_1a_CC2$tide_vol_out)
S3_1a_YC_out_per_tide <- (S3_1a_YC1$tide_vol_out + S3_1a_YC2$tide_vol_out)

S3_proportion_in_YC_1a <- (S3_1a_YC_in_per_tide)/
  (S3_1a_YC_in_per_tide + S3_1a_CC_in_per_tide)
S3_proportion_in_YC_1a 
S3_proportion_out_YC_1a <- (S3_1a_YC_out_per_tide)/
  (S3_1a_YC_out_per_tide + S3_1a_CC_out_per_tide)
S3_proportion_out_YC_1a 


# what is the average area inundated in any tide (average area inundated in general)

mean(Inun_S3$`1A_area_m2`)
# 19.8 ha
```

Scenario 6 has some issues. Let's investigate these line by line in the next chunk.

```{r scenario_6_troubleshoot}
# investigate what's going on with scen6_3a_top_yc which isn't working above
# visualise what a dataset looks like
ggplot(scen6_3a_top_yc, aes(x = Time, y = Flow_m3_15min)) +
  geom_line()
# closer inspection of first 200 points
ggplot(scen6_3a_top_yc[1:200,], aes(x = Time, y = Flow_m3_15min)) +
  geom_line() 

# identify peaks and troughs - issue was that peak heights are much smaller than our original parameter of 50 minpeakheight. remove this parameter and make it 2 instead.
peaks <- findpeaks(scen6_3a_top_yc$Flow_m3_15min, minpeakheight = 2, minpeakdistance = 20)
troughs <- -findpeaks(-scen6_3a_top_yc$Flow_m3_15min, minpeakheight = 2, minpeakdistance = 20) # feed in negative data to find troughs. making them negative again with the negative in front of the function

# when calculating the size of each tide, need to account for the fact this dataset only picks up 26 tides where it should pick up roughly double that, because there are periods where there's little tidal action here. therefore, the average tide is half of what we calculate - accounted for by dividing by 2 for tide_vol_in and tide_vol_out, and peaktime and troughtime, below.
positives <- scen6_3a_top_yc %>% dplyr::filter(Flow_m3_15min>0)
negatives <- scen6_3a_top_yc %>% dplyr::filter(Flow_m3_15min<0)

S6_3A_top_YC <- tibble(ntides = nrow(peaks),
                 tide_vol_in = sum(positives$Flow_m3_15min) / 53,
                 tide_vol_out = sum(negatives$Flow_m3_15min) / 53,
                 tide_net_exchange = tide_vol_in + tide_vol_out)


  
# now do scen 6 3A calculations
  
S6_3A_YC_in_per_tide <- S6_3A_east_YC$tide_vol_in + S6_3A_south_YC$tide_vol_in + S6_3A_tl_YC$tide_vol_in + S6_3A_top_YC$tide_vol_in
S6_3A_YC_out_per_tide <- S6_3A_east_YC$tide_vol_out + S6_3A_south_YC$tide_vol_out + S6_3A_tl_YC$tide_vol_out + S6_3A_top_YC$tide_vol_out
```

#### 2.2.1 Summary calculations for Dtot

Create an output table summarising all information for each scenario.

**Note for denitrification:**

The equation for TOTAL denitrification (Dtot) in the Blue Heart is:

*Log10 (denitrification, mg/m2/h) = 0.6975 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))*

This can be rearranged as:

*denitrification, mg/m2/h = 10\^(0.6975 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L))) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))*

Given we are taking the input nitrate value as a constant of **0.076**, this then becomes:

*denitrification, mg/m2/h = 10\^(0.6975 (log10 (0.076)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))*

By substituting our soil organic carbon value for each of the three elevation classes (High (\>0.75m) = 4.1, Medium (0.5-0.75m) = 11.5, Low (0-0.5m) = 9), we get the following results:

High elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 7.0435*

Medium elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 7.8283*

Low elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 7.5538*

```{r Output_table_setup}

                 Inun_area_high_m2 = double(), # 11

                 #Final_wetland_NOx_kg = double(), # 13
                 #Output_NOx_conc = double(), # 14 
                 Output_vol_YC_m3 = double(), # 15
                 Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 = double(), # 16
                 Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 = double() #, # 17
                 #Final_channel_NOx_conc = double() # 18
                 )
```

Now do calculations for the table.

Note, need to do the final channel concentration separately, so we can account for inputs from multiple wetlands.

```{r Table_mutation}

# mutate columns based on other column values and some generic values for high/med/low denitrification rates
dft2 <- df2 %>% mutate(
                Input_vol_total_m3 = Input_vol_YC_m3 + Input_vol_other_m3, # 5
                Total_input_NOx_kg = Input_conc_NOx_mgL * Input_vol_total_m3 * 1000 / 1000000, # 7 - * 1000 is to convert from m3 to L and /1000000 is to convert from mg to kg
                Denit_potential_kg_12hr = 
             (Inun_area_low_m2 * 7.5538 + 
              Inun_area_med_m2 * 7.8283 +
              Inun_area_high_m2 * 7.0435)/1000000*12, # 12 - / 1000000 is to convert from mg to kg, * 12 is to calculate over a 12 hour period
                Final_wetland_NOx_kg = 
               case_when(Total_input_NOx_kg - Denit_potential_kg_12hr > 0 ~ Total_input_NOx_kg - Denit_potential_kg_12hr,
                         .default = 0), # 13 - resulting NOx concentration is zero if potential denitrification is greater than input NOx
                Output_NOx_conc_mgL = (Final_wetland_NOx_kg*1000000) / (Input_vol_total_m3*1000) # 14 
             )
```

#### 2.2.2 Also do this for Dw (natural denitrification)

Dw excludes denitrification resulting from nitrification-denitrification processes, so represents the amount of NO3 removed from the water column directly.

The equation for NATURAL denitrification (Dw) in the Blue Heart is:

*Log10 (denitrification, mg/m2/h) = 0.7048 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L)) + 0.9286 + (0.0008\*Soil OC%))*

This can be rearranged as:

*denitrification, mg/m2/h = 10\^(0.7048 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L))) + 0.9286 + (0.0008\*Soil OC%))*

Given we are taking the input nitrate value as a constant of **0.076**, this then becomes:

*denitrification, mg/m2/h = 10\^(0.7048 (log10 (0.076)) + 0.9286 + (0.0008\*Soil OC%))*

By substituting our soil organic carbon value for each of the three elevation classes (High (\>0.75m) = 4.1, Medium (0.5-0.75m) = 11.5, Low (0-0.5m) = 9), we get the following results:

High elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 1.3902*

Medium elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 1.4093*

Low elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 1.4028*

We can go straight to the table mutation stage, as the earlier steps filling the rows of the table are independent of the denitrification equation.

Note, need to do the final channel concentration separately, so we can account for inputs from multiple wetlands.

```{r table_mutation}
# mutate columns based on other column values and some generic values for high/med/low denitrification rates
dfw2 <- df2 %>% mutate(
                Input_vol_total_m3 = Input_vol_YC_m3 + Input_vol_other_m3, # 5
                Total_input_NOx_kg = Input_conc_NOx_mgL * Input_vol_total_m3 * 1000 / 1000000, # 7 - * 1000 is to convert from m3 to L and /1000000 is to convert from mg to kg
                Denit_potential_kg_12hr = 
             (Inun_area_low_m2 * 1.4028 + 
              Inun_area_med_m2 * 1.4093 +
              Inun_area_high_m2 * 1.3902)/1000000*12, # 12 - / 1000000 is to convert from mg to kg, * 12 is to calculate over a 12 hour period
                Final_wetland_NOx_kg = 
               case_when(Total_input_NOx_kg - Denit_potential_kg_12hr > 0 ~ Total_input_NOx_kg - Denit_potential_kg_12hr,
                         .default = 0), # 13 - resulting NOx concentration is zero if potential denitrification is greater than input NOx
                Output_NOx_conc_mgL = (Final_wetland_NOx_kg*1000000) / (Input_vol_total_m3*1000) # 14 
             )
```

### 2.3 Resulting overall change in channel water quality

Finally, combine all wetlands in each scenario to calculate the overall channel concentration.

#### 2.3.1 For Dtot

```{r final_WQ_calcs}
dft3 <- dft2 %>% group_by(Scenario) %>% 
  summarise(Output_NOx_kg = sum(Final_wetland_NOx_kg),
            Total_output_vol_YC_m3 = sum(Output_vol_YC_m3),
            Total_input_vol_m3 = sum(Input_vol_total_m3),
            Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 = mean(Channel_vol_no_denit_m3), # all the same
            Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 = mean(Channel_vol_w_denit_m3), # all the same
            Input_conc_NOx_mgL = mean(Input_conc_NOx_mgL), # all the same
  ) %>% 
  mutate(Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL = (Output_NOx_kg*1000000) / (Total_input_vol_m3*1000)) # calculate overall output concentration over all FPs

# add a line for scenario 0 - no floodplains, but still has potential in-channel denitrification
# commenting this out for now since we're currently excluding in-channel denitrification

#dft3 <- dft3 %>% add_row(Scenario = "Scenario 0",
#                       Output_NOx_kg = 0,
#                       Total_output_vol_YC_m3 = 0,
#                       Total_input_vol_m3 = 0,
#                       Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 = 55290,
#                       Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 = 22300,
#                       Input_conc_NOx_mgL = 0.076,
#                       Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL = 0)

dft3 <- dft3 %>% mutate(Final_channel_NOx_conc_mgL = 
               (Channel_vol_no_denit_m3*1000 * Input_conc_NOx_mgL +
               Channel_vol_w_denit_m3*1000 * Input_conc_NOx_mgL + # if assuming no in-channel denitrification, both parts of the channel get the same input NOx concentration. if want to include channel denitrification, replace Input_conc_NOx_mgL here with the below (channel_base_nit_final_conc)
                 #channel_base_nit_final_conc +
               Total_output_vol_YC_m3*1000 * Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL) / ((Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 + Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 + Total_output_vol_YC_m3)*1000))
```

```{r final_WQ_calcs}
# add a line for scenario 0 - no floodplains, but still has potential in-channel denitrification
```

### 2.4 Try other nitrate inputs

Also try for a couple other input nitrate concentrations.

As a refresh, here is the denitrification equation again.

*Log10 (denitrification, mg/m2/h) = 0.6975 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))*

This can be rearranged as:

*denitrification, mg/m2/h = 10\^(0.6975 (log10 (NO3 (mg/L))) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))*

Given we are taking the input nitrate value as a constant of **0.1**, this then becomes:

*denitrification, mg/m2/h = 10\^(0.6975 (log10 (0.1)) + 1.6030 + (0.0062\*Soil OC%))*

By substituting our soil organic carbon value for each of the three elevation classes (High (\>0.75m) = 4.1, Medium (0.5-0.75m) = 11.5, Low (0-0.5m) = 9), we get the following results:

High elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 8.5294*

Medium elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 9.4798*

Low elevation: *denitrification, mg/m2/h = 9.1474*

```{r water_quality_input_0.1}
df4 <- df2 %>% 
  mutate(Input_conc_NOx_mgL = 0.1)

# mutate columns based on other column values and some generic values for high/med/low denitrification rates
df4 <- df4 %>% mutate(
                Input_vol_total_m3 = Input_vol_YC_m3 + Input_vol_other_m3, # 5
                Total_input_NOx_kg = Input_conc_NOx_mgL * Input_vol_total_m3 * 1000 / 1000000, # 7 - * 1000 is to convert from m3 to L and /1000000 is to convert from mg to kg
                Denit_potential_kg_12hr = 
             (Inun_area_low_m2 * 9.1474 + 
              Inun_area_med_m2 * 9.4798 +
              Inun_area_high_m2 * 8.5294)/1000000*12, # 12 - / 1000000 is to convert from mg to kg, * 12 is to calculate over a 12 hour period
                Final_wetland_NOx_kg = 
               case_when(Total_input_NOx_kg - Denit_potential_kg_12hr > 0 ~ Total_input_NOx_kg - Denit_potential_kg_12hr,
                         .default = 0), # 13 - resulting NOx concentration is zero if potential denitrification is greater than input NOx
                Output_NOx_conc_mgL = (Final_wetland_NOx_kg*1000000) / (Input_vol_total_m3*1000) # 14 
             )

df5 <- df4 %>% group_by(Scenario) %>% 
  summarise(Output_NOx_kg = sum(Final_wetland_NOx_kg),
            Total_output_vol_YC_m3 = sum(Output_vol_YC_m3),
            Total_input_vol_m3 = sum(Input_vol_total_m3),

            Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 = mean(Channel_vol_w_denit_m3), # all the same
            Input_conc_NOx_mgL = mean(Input_conc_NOx_mgL), # all the same
  ) %>% 
  mutate(Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL = (Output_NOx_kg*1000000) / (Total_input_vol_m3*1000)) # calculate overall output concentration over all FPs

# add a line for scenario 0 - no floodplains, but still has potential in-channel denitrification

df5 <- df5 %>% add_row(Scenario = "Scenario 0",
                       Output_NOx_kg = 0,
                       Total_output_vol_YC_m3 = 0,
                       Total_input_vol_m3 = 0,
                       Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 = 55290,
                       Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 = 22300,
                       Input_conc_NOx_mgL = 0.1,
                       Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL = 0)

df5 <- df5 %>% mutate(Final_channel_NOx_conc_mgL = 
               (Channel_vol_no_denit_m3*1000 * Input_conc_NOx_mgL +
               Channel_vol_w_denit_m3*1000 * 0 +
               Total_output_vol_YC_m3*1000 * Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL) / ((Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 + Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 + Total_output_vol_YC_m3)*1000))
```

```{r water_quality_input_0.05305}
               (Channel_vol_no_denit_m3*1000 * Input_conc_NOx_mgL +
               Channel_vol_w_denit_m3*1000 * 0 +
               Total_output_vol_YC_m3*1000 * Total_output_NOx_conc_mgL) / ((Channel_vol_no_denit_m3 + Channel_vol_w_denit_m3 + Total_output_vol_YC_m3)*1000))
```

### 2.5 Using the water quality volume approach to calculate denitrification values

For the earlier part of this paper, we calculated denitrification resulting from each scenario. This is different than the water quality calculations, as for water quality, we were focussing on Yandina Creek only so had to take into account volumes coming in and out of Yandina Creek, and only focussed on wetlands attached to Yandina Creek. However, denitrification just cares about the total volume coming into wetlands in each scenario. Therefore, we need volumes in and out of all wetlands from all creeks. We will also use the input NOx concentration of 0.053 for this broader section (not 0.076).

First, need to input data for floodplains and scenarios not considered in the water quality section (because they relate to creeks other than Yandina Creek). Note you have to run all the code above to move into this section, as this section relies on functions and data specified there.

Next, calculate input and output volumes using the methodology above. This time, we don't need to separate Yandina and Coolum Creek/Maroochy River - can just add all flows together.
